hypotheses.justification: In fact hh, ha, and hb can all be deleted simultaneously. For every real x, |min 1 x| ≤ |x|: split into x ≤ 1 and 1 ≤ x. Consequently the norm of the summand is bounded by |(a s * b s) / (h * h)|. This majorant is summable by LengthArea.summable_mul_of_squares, Summable.div_const, and Summable.abs; apply Summable.of_norm_bounded. These lemmas were checked in the sources. No sign or nonzero condition on h is needed; at h = 0 the summands are zero.

For arbitrary real a s, |min 1 (a s / h)| ≤ |a s / h|, by splitting at a s / h = 1. Thus the summand's norm is bounded by |(a s * b s) / (h * h)|. LengthArea.summable_mul_of_squares followed by Summable.div_const and Summable.abs makes this bound summable, so Summable.of_norm_bounded proves the conclusion without ha. This also works without hh and hb, including zero values and empty index types.

The same absolute-value comparison works for arbitrary b s: |min 1 (b s / h)| ≤ |b s / h|. Bound the product's norm by |(a s * b s) / (h * h)| and apply Summable.of_norm_bounded using LengthArea.summable_mul_of_squares, Summable.div_const, and Summable.abs. Hence hb is unnecessary, even simultaneously with ha and hh; zero values and empty index types cause no exception.
